pool.text: Pakistan gained independence, making the southern port city of Karachi its provisional national capital.
A commission was constituted to select a suitable site near Rawalpindi for the national capital.
The commission recommended the area northeast of Rawalpindi which served as the provisional capital.
The master plan for Islamabad was drawn up to integrate Rawalpindi and adjoining areas.
Islamabad was established and replaced Karachi as Pakistan's national capital.
The Children's Hospital was completed as a teaching and doctor training institute.
The Faisal Mosque was built as an iconic cultural and religious landmark.
Shifa International Hospital was founded as a teaching hospital in Islamabad.
Islamabad Stock Exchange was founded as Pakistan's third largest stock exchange.
The South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation summit was hosted in the city.
The city suffered damage from the magnitude 7.6 Kashmir earthquake.
PAEC General Hospital and teaching institute was established, affiliated with the Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission.
The Pakistan Monument was built as a landmark for tourists.
There were 12 hospitals, 76 dispensaries, and five maternity and child welfare centres.
Islamabad was ranked as the best place to start a business in Pakistan.
Four terrorist incidents occurred in the city, killing four people, including the murder of Punjab Governor Salmaan Taseer.
The construction of the Rawalpindi-Islamabad Metrobus began in February.
The first phase of the Metrobus network opened, stretching 22.5 kilometres.
Initial archaeological excavations unearthed the remains of a Buddhist stupa at Ban Faqiran.
The new airport inaugurated on 20 April, spreading over 19 square kilometres.
